info.title: Orion — Declarative Services Runtime API
info.description:
Declarative services runtime platform.

**Authentication.** The admin API (`/api/v2/admin/*`), the Prometheus endpoint (`/metrics`), and the trace read endpoints (`/api/v2/admin/traces*`) require an admin API key when `admin_auth.enabled` is true — the default in the shipped Helm chart and HA compose files. Operations that need it carry a `security` block; see the `admin_bearer` / `admin_api_key` schemes for how the key is presented and for the `admin_auth.header` config key that selects between them.

The data plane (`/api/v2/data/{channel}`) and the health probes are deliberately unauthenticated: channel-level access control is expressed through each channel's `validation_logic` and `origin_allow_list`.

**Errors.** Every non-2xx response uses the `ErrorResponse` envelope: `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}`, plus `details` on validation failures.

post.description: Refuses a raw secret in public_config and a malformed secret locator, then judges the configuration as the node will read it — public_config with each secret reference at its locator path, the references unresolved. Over a built-in driver it is typed and checked as the connector it serves (`http`, `db` or `cache`), exactly as `orion-cli compile` checks it; over an uploaded provider package it must satisfy the package's declared `configuration_schema`. Over a `workflow` provider package, `bindings` must bind each dependency alias the package declares to a stored connection over a built-in or rust provider (the one the dependency names, when it names one), and nothing else; a deployment member for the connection must then require each bound connection. A refusal names each problem by field in `details`. Then persists an immutable, content-addressed connection revision: the same revision with the same content answers it again, with different content it is a conflict.

post.description: Probes the stored revision through the provider it names — nothing in the request can choose another — recorded in the audit log first because it reaches a real backend. Over a built-in driver it connects for real, with the revision's secret references resolved as the node resolves them at load: `org.orion.postgresql`, `org.orion.mysql` and `org.orion.sqlite` run `SELECT 1` through the node's own connector pool (refusing a private address unless `allow_private_urls`); `org.orion.http` resolves the configured URL's host and opens a TCP connection to it (no HTTP request is sent and no credential is presented; the same private-address rule applies); `org.orion.memory-cache` reads a probe key. Over an uploaded provider package it validates the configuration and runs the provider's health check within an admitted run budget. A probe that ran answers `200` whatever it found: `healthy` is the finding, `details.probe` says which check ran and `details.error` why it failed — never a resolved secret.

post.summary: Commit the next deployment revision: an apply or a rollback
post.description: An apply (`manifest` with its `reviewed_manifest_digest`) plans the manifest again, refuses it unless it plans to the digest that was reviewed, and commits it. A rollback (`rollback_to`) commits an earlier revision's manifest as a new revision, re-checking its providers' admissions as of now. Either is a compare-and-swap against `base_revision` in one database transaction, idempotent on `idempotency_key` per principal (a replay answers the receipt it committed), and then reconciles the local node.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description:
Filter by mode: `sync`, `async` or `cron` — the transport the
message arrived on.

parameters.description: Column to sort by: created_at (default), updated_at, status, channel, mode.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Keyset cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor`: pass it back
unmodified. Valid only with the default `created_at` ordering, and
mutually exclusive with `offset`; cheaper than `offset` on a large
table because it never skips rows.

parameters.name: include_total
parameters.description:
Compute `total` for this page (default false). Off by default:
the count is a full scan of the filtered set on Postgres and InnoDB,
paid on every page even though the number rarely changes what the
caller does next.

200.description: Page of traces. Not the common paginated envelope: `total` is present only with `include_total=true`, because the count scans the whole filtered set, and `next_cursor` carries the keyset position of the last row, to pass back as `?cursor=`, when the page is ordered by `created_at` (the default) and may have a successor.

400.description: Malformed cursor, or cursor combined with offset or a non-default sort

get.description:
Fetch one trace. Access follows a two-lane rule: present either a valid admin credential, or — for async submissions — the `trace_token` returned with the 202, in the `x-trace-token` header. Traces without a token (sync traces, DLQ retries, rows from before 1.0.0) are admin-plane only when admin auth is enabled.

The `?token=` query parameter is a **deprecated** alternative for clients that cannot set headers. Prefer the header: a URL is not a private place, and the token leaks into browser history, proxy and CDN logs, `Referer` headers and anywhere a link is pasted. Reads authorised that way answer with a `Deprecation` header.

Every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` — the body is the submission's result and the capability is not an `Authorization` header, so nothing else stops a shared cache storing it.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description:
**Deprecated.** The capability token returned with the async 202. Use
the `x-trace-token` header instead: a URL is not a private place. It
reaches browser history, reverse-proxy and CDN access logs, analytics,
`Referer` headers on anything the page loads next, and every chat
window a support ticket is pasted into — none of which the header
touches. Still accepted for clients that cannot set headers; responses
that authorise this way carry a `Deprecation` header, and
`orion_trace_token_query_reads_total` counts them so an operator can
see whether anything still depends on it.

401.description: Missing or wrong trace token / admin credential

post.description:
Invoke a channel's workflow synchronously.

This is a **templated** path, not a static one. Orion serves the whole data plane from a single catch-all route (`/api/v2/data/{*path}`) and resolves the target channel at request time, so no per-channel path exists in this document:

* **Simple HTTP channels** — a single path segment matched against the channel `name`, e.g. `POST /api/v2/data/order-intake`.
* **REST channels** — each active channel registers its own method and path pattern (`config.rest.routes`) at engine-reload time; those patterns may span several segments and declare their own path parameters, which arrive in the workflow as `metadata.params`, percent-decoded exactly once (`a%2Fb` becomes `a/b`). Static segments match byte-exact — the path is case-sensitive per RFC 3986. Any HTTP method is accepted — `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` behave identically to the `POST` documented here, with the verb exposed as `metadata.http_method`. Query the admin channel API for the routes a given deployment actually serves.

Append `/async` to submit to the queue instead — see `POST /api/v2/data/{channel}/async`.

Authentication is per channel and off by default: `admin_auth` covers the admin plane only. A channel carrying an `auth` block in its config (`api_key` or `hmac`) authenticates every caller on this path and on `/async` alike; a channel without one is open to anyone who can reach the port. `validation_logic` and `origin_allow_list` complement it but are not authentication — `Origin` is client-supplied.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Channel name, or the first segment of a REST channel's registered route pattern.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Set to `1`/`true` to append `_orion.profile` timings to the response. Requires `tracing.debug_profile_enabled = true`; the `X-Orion-Profile` header does the same.

requestBody.description:
Workflow input, in either of two shapes. An object carrying `data` or `metadata` is the **envelope**: `data` is the payload, and `metadata` is merged into the message metadata alongside the server-supplied `channel`, `http_method`, `params`, `query` and `headers` keys. Any other JSON body **is** the payload — `{"amount": 5}` is equivalent to `{"data": {"amount": 5}}`. An empty body is accepted (typical for `GET`/`DELETE` REST channels) and treated as `{"data": {}}`. 

That detection is per channel: a channel configured with `request.body_mode = "payload"` takes the whole body as the payload whatever keys it carries, and accepts no caller-supplied `metadata`. Use it when the request model owns the name `data` — under the default `auto` mode such a body is read as an envelope and its sibling fields are discarded.

200.description: Workflow completed. `errors` is empty on success; when tasks failed it carries sanitized `{code, message, task_id}` entries and the envelope gains a `request_id` for correlation with the persisted trace.

400.description: Malformed JSON body, empty channel segment, an invalid percent-sequence in the request path, or a channel `validation_logic` rejection (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, with per-field `details`)

401.description: The channel declares `auth` and the request did not satisfy it — absent, wrong, or malformed credential. One message for every cause, so a caller cannot learn which half they had right.

403.description: `Origin` header not in the channel's `origin_allow_list`

404.description: No channel serves this request: either no REST route matches the requested method and path, or the single-segment name is not an active channel in the registry.

409.description: Deduplication key already seen inside the channel's dedup window

500.description: Result exceeded `queue.max_result_size_bytes` (`RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`), or an internal failure (`INTERNAL_ERROR`)

503.description: Channel backpressure limit reached, a connector circuit breaker is open (`CIRCUIT_OPEN`), or a rate-limit/dedup backend outage on a channel configured with `on_backend_error = "deny"`

post.description:
Queue a channel's workflow for background execution and return immediately.

Accepts the same body and resolves the channel exactly as `POST /api/v2/data/{channel}` (including REST route patterns — append `/async` to any of them). All ingress guards still apply before the queue hand-off: the origin allow-list, the rate limit, `validation_logic`, deduplication and backpressure. The response cache is sync-only, so an async submission never returns a cached body.

Poll `GET /api/v2/admin/traces/{id}` with the returned `trace_id` for the result, presenting the returned `trace_token` via the `x-trace-token` header or `?token=` query parameter. The token scopes the poll to this submission; an admin credential also works.

`trace_id` is always present. Async submission is a request for a result to be fetched later, so the trace row is written before the 202 is sent even when `trace_storage.mode` is `off` — that setting still applies in full to the synchronous endpoint, where the caller already has the answer.

parameters.description: Channel name, or the first segment of a REST channel's registered route pattern.

requestBody.description: Same envelope as the synchronous endpoint.

202.description: Accepted and queued. `trace_id` and `trace_token` are always present — the trace row is written before this response is sent, so the id can always be polled.

401.description: The channel declares `auth` and the request did not satisfy it — absent, wrong, or malformed credential. One message for every cause, so a caller cannot learn which half they had right.

get.description: Detailed health report. Always reachable, but when `admin_auth.enabled` is true the topology detail (`git_hash`, `build_timestamp`, `workflows_loaded`, the circuit-breaker map, connector load failures and quarantined channels — names and failure reasons) is included only for requests presenting a valid admin credential; anonymous callers get status, version, uptime and coarse per-component states. Probes should use `/healthz` and `/readyz`.

200.description: Service healthy, or degraded with the database reachable

503.description: The database is unreachable; same body shape

get.description: Liveness probe. Returns `200 {"status":"ok"}` as long as the process is running and the HTTP server is accepting connections — it performs no dependency checks, so a database outage must not restart the pod. Use `/readyz` for rotation decisions and `/health` for a detailed report. Unauthenticated, so probes work without provisioning an admin key.

Prometheus exposition endpoint. Registered only when `metrics.enabled` is true — otherwise the path 404s, so a deployment with metrics off is not mistaken for a working scrape target.

On this listener it is guarded by the same admin credential as `/api/v2/admin/*` when `admin_auth.enabled` is true, so scrapers must be configured with the key. Setting `metrics.bind_addr` instead moves the endpoint to a dedicated unauthenticated listener on a private interface and removes it from this one entirely.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin API key. Only returned when `admin_auth.enabled` is true.

get.description:
Readiness probe. Reports `ready` only when the database responds, startup has completed, every background task the node cannot work without is still running. In cluster mode the shared dedup store, response cache and rate limits live in that same database, so its check covers them. The `components.engine` field is a constant `"ok"` kept for response-shape stability: the engine snapshot is lock-free and cannot be unavailable once the process serves.

The `components.background_tasks` is `error` when a required task — the trace dispatcher, the persistence workers, the audit writer, the DLQ retry consumer, the cluster reconciler — has stopped for good; each of those fails silently otherwise, dropping traces or audit rows while the data plane keeps answering 200s. Unauthenticated, so probes work without provisioning an admin key.

503.description: At least one component is not ready — same body shape with `"status":"not_ready"`

AdmitPackageRequest.description:
Request body for admitting an uploaded provider package
(`PUT /api/v2/admin/connector-packages/{digest}/admission`). The body is
optional.

lock.description: The provider lock the admission must verify against.

base_revision.description:
The head the candidate was planned on; anything else is
`DEPLOYMENT_HEAD_CONFLICT`.

reason.description: The audit reason the revision records.

reviewed_manifest_digest.description:
The digest `POST /deployment-plans` answered for this candidate on
this base. A candidate that plans to anything else is
`REVIEWED_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, and nothing is committed.

trace_id.description:
Id to poll via `GET /api/v2/admin/traces/{id}`. Always present: a 202
is a receipt for a result, so the row it names is written before this
response is sent.

trace_token.description:
Capability token scoping the poll to this submission: present
it via the `x-trace-token` header or `?token=` query parameter.
Shown once, here — only its hash is stored.

path.description: Absolute path on the node that served the request.

BackupListItemResponse.description:
One row of `GET /api/v2/admin/backups`. Deliberately not
[`BackupFileResponse`]: the listing reads `mtime` off the directory entry
and has no `path`.

namespace.description: The namespace whose version was bumped.

stores.description:
How many response-cache stores the bump reached: the default store
and each in-memory store on the node that answered. In a cluster the
default store is the shared database, which carries the bump to every
node.

CatalogueEntry.description:
One entry of `GET /api/v2/admin/functions`.

The endpoint used to serve the schema registry directly, which meant it
listed only the functions Orion input-schema validates — 18 of the 27 valid
names, omitting `map`, `filter`, `parse_json` and the rest. Those are the
ones people actually type: in the deployment that reported it (#288) the
nine omitted names were 425 of 631 tasks, `map` alone 310. A completion
source offering the connector functions and none of those is not an
incomplete catalogue, it is the wrong one.

A projection of [`FunctionEntry`] rather than the entry itself, because the
wire shape is pinned by `docs/openapi.json` and the two are allowed to grow
at different rates: `writes` and the connector rule are the analysis's
business and are not served.

input_fields.description:
**Absent**, not null, when the function declares no input schema —
which is the honest JSON encoding of "there is nothing here", and what
a consumer branches on.

retry_safety.description:
What a second run of this function does — see [`RetrySafety`]. Served
for every entry, built-ins included: "is it safe to retry this task?"
is a question about every function a workflow can name, not only the
ones Orion declares an input schema for. `{"kind": …}`: `pure`,
`read`, `idempotent_write`, `unsafe_write`, or `depends_on` with the
`input` that decides it.

source.description:
`orion` for a handler Orion implements and input-schema validates,
`engine` for a dataflow-rs built-in the engine executes itself,
`plugin` for a WebAssembly plugin's function.

ChannelDefinition.description:
A channel: everything but its identity and its workflow, which is the
Workflow its manifest member `requires`.

protocol.description:
The channel driver that serves it (`rest`, `http`, `cron` in
Community), lowercased.

ChannelLoadIssueResponse.description: A channel a generation refused to serve.

channel.description: The channel's name — what the quarantine is keyed by.

channel_id.description: The channel's id. Empty from a server that predates it.

workflow_id.description: The workflow the channel is bound to, when it names one.

found_on_this_node.description:
Whether the breaker existed on the node that served the request.
Breakers are node-local; in cluster mode the reset reaches every node
regardless, so `false` here is not a failure.

enabled.description:
Whether `engine.circuit_breaker.enabled` is set. When false, `breakers`
is empty because nothing is tracked.

scope.description: Always `"node"` — breaker state is per-replica, never cluster-wide.

ConnectionProbeResponse.description:
One health probe of a connection revision
(`POST /api/v2/admin/connections/{id}/revisions/{revision}/probes`). A probe
that ran answers `200` whatever it found: `healthy` is the finding.

driver_id.description: The built-in driver, or the backend id of the provider package.

bindings.description:
Over a `workflow` provider package: the connection each of the
package's dependency aliases calls (`alias -> connection_id`). Empty
for any other provider.

configuration_digest.description:
The digest over the public settings, the locators and the bindings:
what a manifest member for this revision names as its
`definition_digest`.

ConnectionsListResponse.description:
Connection revisions, ordered by connection then revision
(`GET /api/v2/admin/connections`, `GET /api/v2/admin/connections/{id}/revisions`).

ConnectorErrorClass.description: The normalised class of a connector failure.

ConnectorLoadIssueResponse.description: An enabled connector the registry could not load.

connector.description: The connector's name — what workflows reference it by.

ConnectorPackageResponse.description:
One connector provider package and its admission record
(`GET /api/v2/admin/connector-packages/{digest}`).

oneOf.description:
The admission recorded for the package; absent while it was never
admitted.

tier.description:
The tier `distribution.json` declares; `community` when it declares
none.

ConnectorPackagesListResponse.description: Every stored package, and every admission record (`GET /api/v2/admin/connector-packages`).

ConvergenceStatusResponse.description: Node/cluster convergence on a committed deployment revision (`GET /api/v2/admin/deployments/{revision}/convergence`).

CreateConnectionRevisionRequest.description:
Request body to create an immutable connection revision
(`POST /api/v2/admin/connections/{id}/revisions`). The connection is the
one the path names.

bindings.description:
Over a `workflow` provider package: which connection each of the
package's declared dependency aliases calls (`alias -> connection_id`).
Every alias must be bound, and each target must be a stored
connection; a deployment member for this connection must require each
bound connection. Absent means none, as it must be for any other
provider.

public_config.description:
The connection's settings. Never a secret: a credential-shaped key or
value is refused.

revision.description:
The revision to create: one past the highest stored, for a change.
Creating a revision that is stored with the same content answers it
again; with different content, `IMMUTABLE_CONNECTION_CONFLICT`.

secret_locators.description:
Where each credential comes from: a config path (`connection_string`,
`auth.token`, `auth.client_secret`, …) to a secret reference such as
`env://ORDERS_DB_URL`. Placed at that path when the connection is
used. Absent means none.

CreateConnectionRevisionResponse.description:
A created (or, for identical content, the stored) connection revision
(`POST /api/v2/admin/connections/{id}/revisions`, `201`).

CreateDeploymentPlanRequest.description: Request body for planning a candidate deployment (`POST /api/v2/admin/deployment-plans`).

base_revision.description: The head the candidate is planned on: `0` before the first apply.

CreateDeploymentRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/v2/admin/deployments`: commit the next
revision on top of `base_revision`, under compare-and-swap and an
idempotency key. Either a reviewed manifest (an apply) or an earlier
revision to deploy again (a rollback, `rollback_to`).

CreateDeploymentResponse.description:
A committed apply or rollback (`POST /api/v2/admin/deployments`, `202`):
the revision is committed, and nodes converge on it.

evaluation.description:
This node's convergence on the committed revision, after it tried to
build it.

local_error.description:
Why this node could not build the committed revision, when it could
not. The revision stays committed; the node keeps serving what it had.

warnings.description:
What committing this revision does not do — a rollback does not
reverse an external effect already made. Empty for an apply.

CronOccurrenceResponse.description:
One occurrence in full: `GET /api/v2/admin/cron/occurrences/{id}`.

Adds what the summary leaves out — the failure reason, the trace to read the
run in, and the lease bookkeeping that answers "which node has it, and until
when?".

channel_version.description: The channel version that materialised this occurrence…

claimed_by.description:
The instance holding this occurrence, and until when. Both `null` unless
an attempt is in flight.

executing_version.description:
…and the one that claimed it. They differ when the channel gained a
version between the two, which is expected: a pending occurrence follows
the active generation at claim time, exactly as a queued async trace
does. `null` until claimed.

fencing_token.description:
The acquisition generation this attempt holds its key under. Diagnostic:
Orion's connectors do not accept a fencing token, so it bounds Orion's
own writes rather than a downstream side effect.

singleton_slot.description:
Which of the key's `concurrency.slots` this attempt holds, from `0`.
Two occurrences of one key can share a fencing token when they hold
different slots, so the pair is what names a hold. `null` under
`allow`.

trace_id.description:
The trace this attempt wrote, readable at
`GET /api/v2/admin/traces/{id}`. `null` before admission, and when trace
storage dropped the row — the occurrence is kept either way, because it
is scheduling correctness state rather than optional observability.

CronOccurrenceSummaryResponse.description:
One row of `GET /api/v2/admin/cron/occurrences`.

The list projection: what happened and when, without the diagnostic detail.
Narrower than [`CronOccurrenceResponse`] for readability rather than for
cost — an occurrence carries no payload column, unlike a trace — so a page
of a hundred reads as a schedule's history instead of as a wall of lease
bookkeeping.

channel_name.description:
The channel's name when this occurrence was materialised, not its name
now — renaming a channel does not rewrite what already ran.

scheduled_for.description: The immutable UTC instant this occurrence was due.

status.description:
`pending`, `claimed`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`,
`skipped_misfire` or `skipped_singleton`. An open string on the wire:
tolerate a value you do not know.

CronScheduleStatusResponse.description:
One channel's schedule as the runtime sees it right now:
`GET /api/v2/admin/cron/status`.

Deliberately a separate response rather than fields on the channel. The
channel row is an immutable authored definition; where its cursor has got to
is runtime state that changes every minute, and writing it into the active
row would make an immutable record mutable.

last_status.description:
The most recent occurrence's status and instant, so one read answers
"is this schedule healthy?".

next_fire_at.description:
The next UTC instant this schedule will materialise. `null` when the
reconciler has not yet seen the channel — it appears within one poll
interval of activation.

paused_at.description:
Set when the channel has left the active set. Its history is kept; it
simply stops producing occurrences.

pending.description:
Occurrences waiting for a worker. A number that only grows is the signal
that this schedule is producing work faster than the instance runs it.

schedule.description:
The authored expression and zone, echoed so a status read answers
"what is scheduled?" without a second request.

singleton_key.description: The lock this channel's runs take. Present under `forbid`.

slots.description:
How many runs of `singleton_key` this channel admits at once. Present
under `forbid`.

slots_held.description:
Live leases on `singleton_key` right now, across every channel that
shares the key — so it can exceed this channel's `slots` when another
channel declares more, or just after `slots` was lowered.

Definition.description:
One deployable definition, as `POST /api/v2/admin/definitions` takes it
and the artifact store holds it: its kind and the document of that kind.
The artifact's digest covers the whole value, so a manifest member's kind
is bound to the definition it names. Identity is not part of it: a
member's `id` and `revision` say which entity this definition is.

DefinitionAdvisory.description: One advisory on an uploaded definition ([`DefinitionResponse::advisories`]).

check.description:
A stable id for the kind of finding (`engine.unguarded_validation`,
`logic.escaped_template_key`, `engine.advisory`). A later version
may add ids, so this is an identifier, not an enum.

path.description: Where in the definition it was found, as the engine names it.

advisories.description:
What the engine reports about a workflow and does not refuse — a
`$`-prefixed key it emits with one `$` stripped, a `validation` whose
failure stops nothing. Informational: the definition was stored.
Empty for a channel or a plugin.

digest.description:
`sha256:…` of the canonical definition: what a manifest member's
`definition_digest` names.

DeploymentEntityUpdate.description: A member the base deploys at one revision and the candidate at another.

DeploymentManifest.description:
A deployment manifest: the providers a deployment pins and the members
it deploys (`POST /deployment-plans`, `POST /deployments`, and read back
by `GET /deployments/{revision}`).

provider_lock_digest.description:
The digest of the provider lock the providers were resolved under,
when they were.

providers.description:
The uploaded provider packages the members run on. A connection over
a built-in driver needs no entry.

DeploymentPlanResponse.description:
A candidate deployment, checked against its base
(`POST /api/v2/admin/deployment-plans`). Nothing is stored: the plan is a
function of the request and the store, and `reviewed_manifest_digest` is
what an apply must name to commit exactly this candidate.

added_entities.description: Members the base does not deploy at all.

removed_entities.description: Members the base deploys and the candidate drops: they stop serving.

reviewed_manifest_digest.description:
The candidate's canonical manifest digest. An apply names it as its
`reviewed_manifest_digest`.

updated_entities.description: Members the base deploys at another revision.

DeploymentReceiptResponse.description:
The durable receipt of a committed apply or rollback. A replay of the
same idempotency key answers the receipt the first request committed.

principal.description: The admin key id that committed it, or `anonymous`.

receiving_node_id.description: The node that took the write: what `?target=this-node` waits on.

manifest.description: The canonical manifest. A compacted revision's has no members.

DeploymentRevisionResponse.description:
A committed deployment revision with its manifest
(`GET /api/v2/admin/deployments/{revision}`).

DeploymentRevisionSummary.description:
A committed deployment revision without its manifest: one row of
`GET /api/v2/admin/deployments`.

member_count.description: Members in the manifest; `0` once compacted.

members_compacted.description:
The collector dropped this revision's members: it can no longer be
rolled back to.

parent_revision.description: The head it was committed on; absent for the first revision.

DeploymentsPage.description:
One page of committed revisions, newest first, with the head they were
read against (`GET /api/v2/admin/deployments`).

next_cursor.description:
Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next, older page; absent on the last.
Opaque: do not parse it.

older_than_hours.description: Echo of the requested age bound.

EditionFinding.description: One reason a revision cannot move to the target edition.

EditionFindingCode.description: Why an edition transition preflight refuses a revision.

EditionTier.description: An edition, and the distribution tier a provider package declares.

EditionTransitionPreflightRequest.description:
Request body for Enterprise-to-Community edition transition preflight
(`POST /api/v2/admin/edition-transition-preflight`). The body is optional.

revision.description: The revision to inspect; the head when absent.

incompatible_providers.description: `publisher.provider_id` of each provider only Enterprise serves.

EffectStatus.description:
What the host observed of an external effect.

Ordered by uncertainty: once an attempt or a child records
[`EffectStatus::Unknown`], a later local pre-send rejection cannot
downgrade the logical invocation back to [`EffectStatus::NotStarted`].

EngineCapabilities.description: Node capabilities a plan can predict quarantines from.

cron.description: `cron.enabled`: whether this node schedules cron channels.

plugins.description: `plugins.enabled`: whether this node runs the plugin sandbox.

EngineLoadIssues.description: What a runtime generation could not load, on the node that answered.

oneOf.description:
What this node is configured to run. `None` from a server that
predates the field.

channels.description: Distinct channel names across the loaded workflows.

generation.description: The id of the generation this node serves.

oneOf.description:
What that generation could not load. `None` from a server that
predates the field.

EntityKind.description: The kind of a deployment member.

ErrorDetail.description:
The object under the `error` key.

Serialization matches the server's v1.0 behaviour exactly: `details` is
omitted when empty (clients expecting only the v0.1 `{code, message}`
envelope still parse), `request_id` is omitted when the request had none.
Deserialization defaults every field so a pre-1.0 body still reads.

ErrorFieldDetail.description:
Per-field validation detail returned in the `error.details[]` array.

`code` is a stable machine-readable identifier from [`field_codes`].

`path` is a pointer to the offending field, and is rooted one of two ways
depending on how far the request got:

- **Validation reached** — the path is resource-rooted and may be indexed:
  `channel.protocol`, `tasks[2].function.input.connector`.
- **The body failed to deserialize** — validation never ran, so the layer
  that reports it knows the field name but not which resource was being
  parsed. The path is `body.<field>`, or bare `body` when even the field
  cannot be recovered from the parser's message.

Match on the trailing segment rather than the whole path if you need to
treat both the same way.

HealthResponse.description:
`GET /health`: the detailed report. The fields after `components` are
served only to a caller that may read the admin plane.

background_tasks.description: Each background task's state and restarts.

components.description:
Per-subsystem state, each `ok`, `degraded`, `error` or `disabled`:
`database`, `engine`, `connectors`, `channels`, `background_tasks`,
`engine_reload`, `plugins`, and `cron` when this node schedules.

connectors.description: The breaker map (node-local) and the connectors that failed to load.

cron.description: The scheduler's own health, on a node that schedules.

git_hash.description: Build provenance and detail, served only to an admin caller.

plugins.description: The plugins loaded, and those that failed to.

ImplementationKind.description:
The three connector implementation kinds.

Channels are not among them: a channel is a native ingress or scheduler
driver, whereas a connector provider may be a Rust driver, a
workflow-group composite, or a Wasm component.

LintResponse.description:
A provider package's lint report (`POST /api/v2/admin/authoring/lint`):
`200` when it is valid, `422` when it is not, `400` when a file does not
decode.

oneOf.description:
The implementation kind `connector.json` declares; absent when it
could not be read or is not one of the kinds.

provider_id.description:
The provider id `connector.json` declares; absent when it could not
be read.

version.description:
The version `connector.json` declares; absent when it could not be
read.

ManifestMember.description:
One member of a manifest: an entity at a revision, the definition (or,
for a connection, the configuration) it is, and what it needs.

definition_digest.description:
A workflow, channel or plugin's stored definition; a connection
revision's `configuration_digest`.

owning_package.description:
The provider package (by digest, one of the manifest's `providers`)
that owns this member. Absent for a member no package owns.

requires.description:
The members this one needs, each at the revision it uses. Absent
means none.

rollouts.description:
A channel's workflow rollout: disjoint bucket intervals covering
`[0, 100)`. Absent means the channel serves one workflow revision.

ManifestProvider.description:
One provider a manifest pins: a publisher, an id, a semantic version
and the package digest.

applied_manifest_digest.description: The manifest digest of the applied revision; absent before one.

applied_revision.description: The revision the node serves; `0` before it served any.

configuration_degraded.description: Whether some member of the applied revision is quarantined.

desired_revision.description: The revision the node is converging on.

last_error.description:
Why the last attempt to build the desired revision failed, while it
does.

retained_revisions.description: The revisions the node keeps built, ascending.

files.description: The package's files, `inventory.json` included, ready for upload.

PackageArtifactState.description: Where a stored provider package's bytes are in their lifecycle.

Paginated_AuditLogEntryResponse.description:
The paginated envelope: `data` plus the three counters, and nothing else.

This is the shape every admin list endpoint returns **except the trace
list** — read that one with [`TracePage`], not this type. `total` here is a
plain `i64` and defaults to `0`, so a body that legitimately omits the field
would read as "zero rows matched" rather than "not counted".

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, ignoring `limit`/`offset`.

Paginated_CronOccurrenceSummaryResponse.description:
The paginated envelope: `data` plus the three counters, and nothing else.

This is the shape every admin list endpoint returns **except the trace
list** — read that one with [`TracePage`], not this type. `total` here is a
plain `i64` and defaults to `0`, so a body that legitimately omits the field
would read as "zero rows matched" rather than "not counted".

items.description:
One row of `GET /api/v2/admin/cron/occurrences`.

The list projection: what happened and when, without the diagnostic detail.
Narrower than [`CronOccurrenceResponse`] for readability rather than for
cost — an occurrence carries no payload column, unlike a trace — so a page
of a hundred reads as a schedule's history instead of as a wall of lease
bookkeeping.

channel_name.description:
The channel's name when this occurrence was materialised, not its name
now — renaming a channel does not rewrite what already ran.

scheduled_for.description: The immutable UTC instant this occurrence was due.

status.description:
`pending`, `claimed`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`,
`skipped_misfire` or `skipped_singleton`. An open string on the wire:
tolerate a value you do not know.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, ignoring `limit`/`offset`.

Paginated_TraceDlqSummaryResponse.description:
The paginated envelope: `data` plus the three counters, and nothing else.

This is the shape every admin list endpoint returns **except the trace
list** — read that one with [`TracePage`], not this type. `total` here is a
plain `i64` and defaults to `0`, so a body that legitimately omits the field
would read as "zero rows matched" rather than "not counted".

items.description:
One row of the DLQ listing: [`TraceDlqEntryResponse`] minus the payloads.

The two differ on purpose — a listing that carried `payload_json` would
return every failed request's body in one response.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, ignoring `limit`/`offset`.

PluginDefinition.description:
A WebAssembly plugin: its `plugin.toml` manifest as JSON and the
component itself, so one digest covers both.

signature.description: A detached Ed25519 signature over the component digest, base64.

PluginLoadIssueResponse.description: A plugin version a generation could not load.

ProbeDetails.description: Which check a probe ran, and why it failed when it did.

oneOf.description:
Whether the failed check may have reached the backend, when a
provider answered it.

error.description: Why it failed; absent when it passed. Never a resolved secret.

oneOf.description: The failure's normalised class, when a provider answered one.

probe.description:
The check: `configuration`, `SELECT 1`, `TCP connect to the URL's
host`, `cache read of a probe key`, `provider health check`.

metadata.description: Merged into the message metadata alongside the server-supplied keys.

ProcessResponse.description:
Synchronous data-plane response envelope.

Deserializable under `cfg(test)` with `deny_unknown_fields`, so
`sync::tests` can round-trip what `response_envelope` actually emits back
through this struct. A field added to the envelope and not to the mirror —
or vice versa — fails the test instead of shipping a spec that describes a
shape nothing sends.

_orion.description:
Debug namespace, present only when profiling was requested and
`tracing.debug_profile_enabled` is on. Currently carries `profile`.

data.description: Workflow output. Shape is entirely channel-defined.

errors.description: Sanitized per-task failures. Empty on a clean run.

id.description: Engine message id, also the correlation key inside the persisted trace.

request_id.description:
Correlation id, present only when `errors` is non-empty: the full
messages are kept in the trace, not returned to the caller.

status.description:
Always `ok` — task-level failures are reported in `errors`, not by
flipping this field.

ProcessTaskError.description:
One task failure, with the message replaced by a generic string — upstream
URLs, connector names, and driver errors stay in the trace.

message.example: Task processing failed; full detail is available in the trace

admission_fingerprint.description:
Changes when the policy or the package's verified inputs do: an
admission recorded under another fingerprint is invalid.

driver_id.description:
The backend id: a `rust` driver's id, or a `workflow`/`wasm`
package's digest.

package_digest.description:
A built-in driver's fixed provider digest — what a connection
revision over it names as its `provider_digest`. Absent for a
backend that is not a built-in driver.

older_than_hours.description:
Age cut-off in hours: exhausted entries whose `failed_at` is older than
this are deleted. Required rather than defaulted — purging is
destructive and an omitted age must not silently mean "everything".

QuarantinedEntity.description: A member the node serves without, and why.

engine.description:
Always `ok`: the engine snapshot is lock-free and cannot be
unavailable once the process serves. Kept for shape stability.

initialized.description: Whether startup has completed, `[packages] apply` included.

ReadinessResponse.description: `GET /readyz`: whether this node should take traffic.

RevokePackageRequest.description:
Request body for revoking an admitted provider package
(`POST /api/v2/admin/connector-packages/{digest}/revocations`). The body
is optional.

reason.description: The reason the request gave, if it gave one.

RollbackDeploymentRequest.description:
Commit an earlier revision's manifest again, as a new revision. It is
re-checked as of now: a provider revoked since is refused.

base_revision.description: The current head; anything else is `DEPLOYMENT_HEAD_CONFLICT`.

reason.description: The audit reason the revision records; `rollback` when absent.

rollback_to.description: The committed revision whose manifest to deploy again.

RolloutInterval.description:
One half-open bucket interval `[start_bucket, end_bucket)` of a
channel's rollout, served by `workflow_revision`.

RuntimeCapabilitiesResponse.description: What this node is and serves (`GET /api/v2/admin/runtime-capabilities`).

admission_policy_id.description: The package admission policy this node admits under.

api_version.description:
The contract revision this server speaks: [`API_VERSION`] of the
`orion-api` it was built with. A client that speaks another must
not read the rest of this answer, or any other v2 answer.

channel_drivers.description: The channel protocols this node serves (`rest`, `http`, `cron`, …).

node_status.description: This node's reconciler: what it serves and how it got there.

provider_backends.description: Every connector provider backend this node registers.

wasm_worlds.description: The WebAssembly plugin worlds this node runs.

ScaffoldRequest.description: Request body to scaffold a new provider package (`POST /api/v2/admin/authoring/scaffold`).

version.description: The package's semantic version; `1.0.0` when absent.

files.description: Relative path → the file, as UTF-8 text or `base64:<…>`.

package_digest.description: The digest the files pack to.

TestDefinitionRequest.description:
`POST /api/v2/admin/definitions/test`: run a workflow definition once on
the node's engine, against live connectors, without deploying it.

definition.description: The workflow to run, as `POST /definitions` would take it.

metadata.description:
The message's metadata, normalised the way an ingress builds it;
empty when absent.

TestDefinitionResponse.description: One run of a workflow definition (`POST /api/v2/admin/definitions/test`).

error.description: Why the run stopped short, when it did.

errors.description: The errors the engine recorded on the message, as it records them.

matched.description: Whether the workflow's condition matched the supplied input.

output.description: The message data after the pipeline ran.

trace.description:
The engine's trace of the run: the context it started from
(`initial`), then each step with its `task_id`, `result`
(`executed` | `skipped` | `failed`) and the changes it made. Its
shape is dataflow-rs's, so it is carried as the engine writes it.

TraceDetailResponse.description: `GET /api/v2/admin/traces/{id}` — the list row plus the payloads.

message.description:
The full engine message. Present only when `status = "completed"`.
`context.metadata` is stripped from the projection.

task_trace_json.description: Per-task execution trace, when the channel enabled `task_details`.

TraceDlqEntryResponse.description: One DLQ entry with its failed payload — `GET`/`requeue` on a single id.

TraceDlqSummaryResponse.description:
One row of the DLQ listing: [`TraceDlqEntryResponse`] minus the payloads.

The two differ on purpose — a listing that carried `payload_json` would
return every failed request's body in one response.

TraceListItem.description:
One row of `GET /api/v2/admin/traces` — payload-free by design.

The narrower sibling of the single-trace read, for the same reason
[`TraceDlqSummaryResponse`] is narrower than [`TraceDlqEntryResponse`]: a
listing that carried `input_json`/`result_json` would return every
caller's request body and the full engine message in one response. The
server's `SELECT` already omits those columns, so this type is the second
half of that guarantee rather than a filter applied after the fact.

Published as `TraceListItem`, the name the spec has always used for this
component: the Rust type gained the `…Response` suffix every dto here
carries, but a component rename would break clients generated against the
old spec — the upgrade guide tracks those as a compat surface.

channel.description: Channel name as it was when the trace ran — a snapshot, not a key.

TracePage_TraceListItem.description:
The trace list's envelope, which [`Paginated`] cannot represent.

`GET /api/v2/admin/traces` differs from every other list in two ways, both
deliberate and both invisible to `Paginated`:

- **`total` is opt-in.** Counting rows across a large trace table is the
  expensive half of the query, so it is computed only for
  `?include_total=true` and the key is otherwise absent. Read through
  `Paginated` that absence becomes `0` — indistinguishable from an empty
  result, and the reason this type exists.
- **`next_cursor` may be present.** The trace list pages by keyset, not by
  offset; when more rows follow, this carries the cursor to pass as
  `?cursor=`. `Paginated` drops the field silently.

items.description:
One row of `GET /api/v2/admin/traces` — payload-free by design.

The narrower sibling of the single-trace read, for the same reason
[`TraceDlqSummaryResponse`] is narrower than [`TraceDlqEntryResponse`]: a
listing that carried `input_json`/`result_json` would return every
caller's request body and the full engine message in one response. The
server's `SELECT` already omits those columns, so this type is the second
half of that guarantee rather than a filter applied after the fact.

Published as `TraceListItem`, the name the spec has always used for this
component: the Rust type gained the `…Response` suffix every dto here
carries, but a component rename would break clients generated against the
old spec — the upgrade guide tracks those as a compat surface.

channel.description: Channel name as it was when the trace ran — a snapshot, not a key.

next_cursor.description:
Keyset cursor for the next page; `None` on the last page. Opaque —
pass it back as `?cursor=`, do not parse it.

total.description:
Present only when the request asked for it with `?include_total=true`.
`None` means "not counted", never "no rows".

UploadPackageRequest.description:
A provider package's files: the body of `POST /api/v2/admin/connector-packages`,
`/authoring/lint` and `/authoring/pack`.

admit.description:
Upload only: admit the package in the same request. Absent means
`false`.

files.description: Relative path → the file, as UTF-8 text or `base64:<…>`.

lock.description:
Upload only, with `admit`: the provider lock the admission must
verify against.

oneOf.description: The admission, when the upload asked for one.

WorkflowDefinition.description:
A workflow: the dataflow-rs workflow document without what the deployment
supplies (`id`, `version`, `channel`, `status` and `rollout`).

condition.description: JSONLogic deciding whether the workflow matches a message.

loop.description: The workflow loop, when the steps repeat.

on_failure.description: What a failing task does to the run.

priority.description: Higher is evaluated first among the workflows of one channel.

tasks.description: The steps: tasks and task groups.

WorkflowOnFailure.description: A workflow's failure policy, the engine's own vocabulary.

admin_api_key.name: X-API-Key
admin_api_key.description: Alternative to `admin_bearer`, active when `admin_auth.header` names a header other than `Authorization`. The raw key is sent as that header's value with no `Bearer ` prefix. `X-API-Key` is the conventional choice and is what this document shows, but the header name is deployment-specific — substitute whatever `admin_auth.header` is set to. Exactly one of the two schemes is live at a time; they are listed as alternatives because this document is generated without knowledge of a deployment's config.

admin_bearer.description: Admin API key presented as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` — the default. Enforced on `/api/v2/admin/*`, `/metrics`, and `/api/v2/admin/traces*` whenever `admin_auth.enabled` is true, which the shipped Helm chart and HA compose files set. Keys come from `admin_auth.api_keys`, either in plaintext or as `sha256:<64-hex>` digests. The data plane (`POST /api/v2/data/{channel}`) is not covered by this scheme.
